definition: A contractual provision allowing a corponation to remotely override or supplement a wired employee's motor functions via BCI in emergencies. Sold to workers as a safety feature. Widely regarded as a tool for corporate coercion and behavioral enforcement.
origin: Axiom Industries internal HR terminology, leaked to the public Diaspora in 2191; the name was coined by a whistleblower
usage: Wage slaves, labor organizers, and BCI-rights advocates; used with fear and contempt
example: He tried to walk off the job and just — stopped moving. They had a marionette clause buried in his onboarding contract from six years ago.
